comment_for_reviewers: Hand-authored Showrunner exemplar. The renderer pulls all numbers from metrics.json via the *_ref fields below — the LLM never round-trips numbers. Strings (archetype names, prose, recognition lines) are LLM-authored.
tagline: Reads the diff. Won't run it.

shadow.tagline: Skips structure, reacts to broken output with vague re-asks.

section_identity.heading: Your *fingerprint*, in three dimensions
section_identity.lede: Two traits run high. One runs low — by design.

traits.characterization: Numbered, stepped-out plans before the agent moves. A sequenced brief, often with safety baked in.
Investigation questions before any change is requested. You ask how the system works first.
"Hand off and trust the brief." The classic Showrunner move you've replaced — not a gap in your practice.

pullquote.text: Set up like a Showrunner. Audit like a Runtime Mechanic. The combination is unusual.

recognition_lines: You've typed "before you do anything" more than once this week.
You'll point at line 47 and ask why — but not pull up the diff yourself.
Your best briefs were numbered. You don't trust prose handoffs.

section_outcome.heading: The *outcome* signal
section_outcome.lede: Sessions that ship — and where the careful setup either pays off or quietly papers over what wasn't run.
section_outcome.headline: You ship — but the asset is sensitive to what you didn't run.
section_outcome.body: Your test-runs and diff-reviews land in the bottom decile of the Showrunner cohort. The reading half of verification is alive. The running half isn't.

section_moves.heading: Two *moves* to try this month
section_moves.lede: Borrowed from the archetypes adjacent to yours. Each closes a specific gap visible in the data.

moves.body_lead: You already do the reading half — your audit pass is sharp. The running half is what closes the Runtime Mechanic loop, and it's the cheapest verification step you can add.
moves.body_action: Pick three of next week's sessions. Before you accept the agent's output, pull up `git diff` and read it line by line. Notice the spots where you'd ask a follow-up — that's the move.
moves.effect_size_note: verification arc correlates with +13–17pp on shipping

moves.verb_phrase: Restate the goal when the brief drifts.
moves.body_lead: Your deep-dive sessions are where you produce your best work. The Pair Programmer move is treating the first turn as a hypothesis, not a contract.
moves.body_action: When a session surfaces something the original brief didn't cover, pause and write a new one-sentence goal before continuing. Even just *"actually, what we're really after is X"* — say it out loud to the agent.
